key_insight: AegisDx reframes AI diagnosis as a safety-oriented reasoning workflow, using structured checks to broaden differentials, surface “must-not-miss” conditions, and verify evidence before suggesting next steps.
clinical_relevance: In acute care, this approach may reduce missed high-risk diagnoses and produce more transparent, clinically useful decision support than a one-shot LLM prediction.
method: Coordinates multiple LLM roles with explicit contracts
Uses structured intermediate outputs and evidence retrieval
Adds verification gates for dangerous diagnoses and reasoning checks
evidence_signal: Across literature cases and emergency department notes, AegisDx outperformed standalone or comparator LLM setups in Top-3 accuracy and improved physician-rated safety, including better capture of must-not-miss conditions.
watch_item: Results are promising but still depend on workflow integration, evidence retrieval quality, and careful validation before real-world clinical deployment.
paper_title: A safety-oriented hypothetico-deductive framework for AI-assisted differential diagnosis
